summary: Discovery focused on latency & throughput for conversational retail assistant. Customer targets: p95 < 400ms for short prompts, support 100 concurrent streaming sessions with token/sec profiling. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS requirements, and next steps to run an on-sample benchmark.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining. I'm Alex, i'll kick us off. we have Samir from the infra/SE side. how's everyone doing?
00:08 Priya Nair (ML Eng): hi yep good, thanks. we really wanna dig into latency and throughput numbers today, and figure out if Redwood can hit our p95 SLOs for the retail recommender chat.
00:18 Mark Holloway (Eng Manager): morning. main thing for us is p95 and concurrency—peak during flash sales can be rough. we want streaming for progressive UI, and need stable token/sec throughput.
00:30 Samir Rao (SE): great—i'll jump in with details. quick qual q: do you plan to use our Hosted API first or you're leaning toward Dedicated/private from day one?
00:40 Luis Ortega (Infra): leaning Dedicated or Private eventually. we have strict data residency and internal audit demands; but for pilots we might use Hosted to move faster.
00:48 Alex Chen (AE): that's common. for latency: are you measuring from our API edge to the client, or from server-to-server?
00:55 Priya Nair: from client p95 end-to-end ideally, but we can provide server-side numbers too. Our target: p95 under 400ms for short prompts (~20 tokens), and p95 under 800ms for 200 token responses. concurrency target is 100 concurrent streaming sessions at peak.
01:12 Samir Rao: ok that's helpful. quick note: our p95 depends on model variant, quantization, and batching policy. for Hosted we typically see p95 ~150-300ms for short 1-2 token generation steps on smaller open models—but depends. for larger models it rises. for streaming the first token latency and chunk cadence matter.
01:33 Mark Holloway: what about token/sec? we need sustained token/sec per GPU to size Dedicated pools.
01:40 Samir Rao: typically we benchmark tokens/sec at different batch sizes. e.g., on a A100-style instance with our optimized runtime, a 7B model might do ~800-1,200 tokens/sec single-stream, higher with batching. 13B drops to ~300-600 tokens/sec depending on quantization. again this is noisy without your prompt distribution.
02:00 Priya: our prompts vary—short product lookup prompts (~10-30 tokens) are most common; occasional long context conversations up to 1k tokens as history, but responses are usually 50-200 tokens. we can share a sample distribution.
02:12 Alex: please do. that lets Samir pick kernels/quant profiles.
02:18 Luis: another constraint—egress bandwidth and NAT gateway throttles in our VPC. if we run Private we have to ensure the model runtime isn't blocked by egress.
02:27 Samir: noted. Private mode can be configured without external egress if you want on-prem; for VPC we support customer-managed NAT and VPC endpoints. encryption with KMS/HSM is supported.
02:36 Mark: security check—do you have SOC2 and can you support SSO/SAML?
02:41 Alex: yes SOC2 Type II, SSO/SAML and RBAC. we'll send the security pack after the call.
02:47 Priya: great. back to p95: do you do prefix/KV caching? some of our queries repeat a lot—would that help for token/sec and latency?
02:55 Samir: absolutely. we have prefix and KV caching to shorten the compute path—especially useful for repeated prompts and few-shot templates. caching can reduce p95 significantly.
03:04 Priya: if we want streaming with early tokens in 100ms p95, is that realistic?
03:09 Samir: depends. for very short prompts and small models + caching, 100-150ms first-token p95 is achievable on Dedicated in many regions. Hosted has similar numbers but depends on multitenancy and instance pool load. For Private or on-prem you can tune further.
03:24 Mark: what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated? say we need consistent p95 at peak.
03:30 Alex: Hosted is great for pilot and early scale; Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs, predictable throughput and lower p95 variance. Private adds full isolation for data controls. Pricing/tickets trade off.
03:41 Mark: ok we care about variance—peaks every day at 10am PST. can Dedicated autoscale quickly?
03:48 Samir: Dedicated supports configurable autoscale and burst pools. you can reserve baseline capacity for steady load and burst into a shared pool or pre-provision burst nodes. scaling times depend on instance type but we have options to pre-warm and keep warm replicas.
04:02 Priya: about benchmarking—we want Redwood to run a token/sec benchmark on our sample queries. can you simulate 100 concurrent streaming sessions and report p50/p95/p99 and token/sec?
04:12 Alex: yes we can. typical deliverable is a 48-72 hour run with your prompt set and concurrency profile—Samir will run it and share results + recommended Dedicated sizing.
04:22 Samir: i have a checklist—sample prompts, target SLOs (p95 numbers), expected concurrency pattern (burst duration), and network topology. i'll also need an account to run the tests or we'll run them in our Hosted env with your data scrubbed.
04:36 Luis: we prefer testing in our VPC or Dedicated to reflect egress. can Redwood's benchmark run inside our VPC?
04:42 Samir: yes for Dedicated/Private we can orchestrate the benchmark inside your VPC using our private agents; for Hosted we run from our endpoints which may not reflect NAT issues.
04:51 Priya: what about streaming chunk sizes? our UI expects 20 token chunks. will that blow up latency?
04:57 Samir: chunk size affects throughput vs latency. smaller chunks mean more frequent flushes but slightly higher per-token overhead. With our runtime we tune to balance: 20-token chunks is common and fine. You'll want to instrument client-side to buffer and display progressively.
05:12 Alex: quick note on metrics—our Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and you can set p95 alerts and regression triggers tied to prompt sets.
05:22 Mark: good. can you explain quantization tradeoffs for p95 vs token/sec? we worry about quality regressions.
05:29 Samir: sure. 8-bit or 4-bit quant reduces memory and increases throughput; 4-bit (LLM.int8/QLoRA-style) can be 2-3x faster token/sec but sometimes affects perplexity or generation artifacts. We recommend running an eval set to compare quality vs latency. Our Optimize toolkit suggests quant profiles based on your acceptance thresholds.
05:51 Priya: we'll need to keep a set of eval prompts and baseline generation scores, yes.
05:56 Samir: perfect. also rollouts: you can pin a model and do canary traffic or an A/B to compare quantized vs full precision. if p95 spikes, automatic fallback to safer model variants is supported.
06:10 Mark: what about model warm-up and KV cache priming—how long does warm-up take?
06:16 Samir: warm-up time depends on model size and sequence length; small models warm in seconds, larger models with huge KV caches can take minutes. you can pre-warm key routes. for Dedicated we can keep warm replicas to avoid cold starts.
06:28 Luis: any infra specifics—GPU types you recommend for 13B vs 70B?
06:33 Samir: 13B usually fine on A100 40GB or equivalent, and 70B often needs multi-GPU setups or quantized runtimes on 80GB-class GPUs. We’ll provide recommended instance types once we see your token distribution.
06:45 Priya: for the benchmark, our targets: p95 <= 400ms short prompts, <= 800ms long responses, sustain 100 concurrent streaming users with 20-token chunks, and measure token/sec across models 7B/13B.
06:58 Samir: noted. we'll aim to show p50/p95/p99 and token/sec, plus CPU/network time breakdown.
07:04 Alex: i'll send the Dedicated pricing+burst sheet and SOC2 pack after call.
07:09 Mark: thanks. a few quick follow-ups—does Redwood log full prompts? we need minimal data retention for PII.
07:17 Alex: by default hosted logs are retained for X days, but you can configure minimal retention or opt-in for no retention. For Dedicated/Private you control retention and KMS. we also offer encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.
07:31 Luis: good. for Private/on-prem we have an HSM for key storage; do you integrate with third-party HSMs?
07:36 Samir: yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM flows; we'll include integration notes in the security docs.
07:43 Priya: what about observability during the benchmark—can we get per-token traces?
07:49 Samir: we emit per-request traces and token latency histograms. high detail logs can be toggled for the benchmark.
07:55 Mark: any gotchas around HTTP/2 or gRPC streaming? we use HTTP/2 in our frontend.
08:01 Samir: we support HTTP/2 and chunked streaming. client implementations vary; we'll share docs with best practices to avoid head-of-line blocking.
08:12 Alex: ok i'm gonna open up for any other questions—Priya?
08:15 Priya: is there an SLA for p95 on Dedicated?
08:18 Alex: Dedicated plans have SLA-backed uptime and we can negotiate latency SLOs in enterprise contracts depending on reserved capacity.
08:25 Priya: perfect. also is there a cost delta for streaming vs non-streaming?
08:29 Alex: streaming cost typically billed per-token similarly, but there's some operational overhead; we'll show estimated cost in the pricing sheet with examples for streaming patterns.
08:39 Luis: when you run benchmarks, do you include KV-cache primed vs cold runs? we want both numbers.
08:44 Samir: yes we'll run both cold and warmed cache scenarios and provide delta analysis.
08:50 Mark: timeline—can you run the benchmarks next week?
08:54 Samir: yes if we get prompts and network details by Friday we can start early next week.
08:59 Alex: sounds good. i'll send items to Priya and Luis now.
09:04 Priya: thanks. one last thing—we sometimes need deterministic generations for replays. how does Redwood handle seeding and determinism across quantized variants?
09:14 Samir: determinism is tricky across quantization and kernel changes; we provide deterministic mode but across quantized vs fp models you may see divergence. for replayable logs we recommend capturing the response with seed and model version pinned.
09:29 Mark: ok thanks.
09:32 Alex: any other blockers?
09:34 Priya: none. we'll share prompts and SLO doc.
09:37 Alex: perfect. recap quickly—next steps: send pricing and security docs, Samir to run 48–72h benchmark in Dedicated/VPC if possible, customer to share prompts and topology, schedule technical deep dive.
09:51 Mark: sounds good. thanks everyone.
09:55 End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap and mis-attributions; some technical terms may be slightly garbled (e.g., K V cache vs KV cache).
